sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Ezard, Bryan. 1997. A grammar of Tawala, an Austronesian language of the Milne Bay area, Papua New Guinea (Pacific Linguistics C-137). Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Proxy only, not a Haigwai source: Tawala is the best-described Taupota-family language and Lithgow's Naura list shares 70% cognates with Tawala (Rabe). Its stress section would give the family pattern to compare against if a Haigwai wordlist with stress marks ever surfaces. Open on ANU (handle 1885/145950); not downloaded because it does not describe Haigwai.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog, resources in and about the Haigwai language [hgw] (as of 2025-01-23), Internet Archive copy of language-archives.org/language/hgw
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalog only. Lists one lexical resource (SIL wordlist oai:sil.org:85579, 'Gweda [grw] Wordlist Milne Bay Province', Alemán, Keilah & Rueck 1997, offline) and no language description of any kind besides the Glottolog pointer; no SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet exists for Haigwai. Other names: Garaghwaghi, Kapulika, Naura.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of Western Melanesia (Pacific Linguistics C-98). Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Only 'Garuwahi' (= Gweda [grw], source 'SIL' wordlist) appears, in Papuan Tip sound-correspondence tables (pp. c. 191-198); Naura/Haigwai/Garughwahi not mentioned anywhere (text a full-text search for stress/accent). No stress statement for any Papuan Tip language; the only stress passages concern Ali/Schouten lenition and orthographic conventions.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. Austronesian languages: Milne Bay and adjacent islands (Milne Bay Province). In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 441-523. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey of ~150 wordlists. Haigwai appears only as the 'Naura' dialect of Taupota (sec. 29, p. 455: Taupota spoken 'at the head of Milne Bay at Waiema, Laviam, Maiwala, Yanianini, and Naura'; Naura 60% with Taupota, 70% with Tawala) and in the Taupota-family cognate table (sec. 53, p. 460). Sec. 84 STRESS (p. 475) is a Papuan-Tip-Cluster-wide remark: constant vowel lengthening near the end of the phonological word; stress phonemic in Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima (and probably Nimowa, Sud-Est); 'In all of the languages of PTC it seems that stress is predictable within certain word-classes,…

sources.citation: Cooper, Mary, Bethwyn Evans & Marie Keilah. 1997. A Rapid Assessment Report on the Garughwahi (Haigwai) Language: Naura and Kapulika Villages. Ms. 17 pp. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only work in any catalog devoted to Haigwai (Glottolog 147394: wordlist + sociolinguistic). SIL rapid-assessment reports of this period sometimes carry a one-paragraph phonology note with a stress remark; it is also the source of the ASJP list. Held at SIL Ukarumpa and in Hammarström's bibliography files (papua\cooperetal_haigwai1997.zip); not in SIL's public archive and no online copy found.
